{{Quote|This isn't a bad armor, but it has one basic flaw: the tracking system alarm.|Jatras, on the Cresh Luck Armor|<ref name="GG" />}}
The '''Cresh Luck Armor''' was a modified [[Creshaldyne Industries/Legends|Creshaldyne Industries]] [[MK.IV riot armor|Riot Armor]] available to the public during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. It protected the wearer against attacks, and it also warned against incoming fast movements in a short range, using an [[Infrared Motion Sensor Array]]. The warning was an audible signal that could be re-directed to sound only in the wearer's [[Blast helmet/Legends|blast helmet]] but, as noticed by user [[Jatras]], locating the attacker would then be harder as the wearer could not use hearing to do so. Other users, such as [[Heller]], changed the warning display so it would not be an intrusive noise.

The Cresh Luck Armor could be bought through [[Gundark's Gear Datalog]]. A number of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], including [[Gennan Var]], used these armors during their chases.

==Description==
{{Quote|The tracking system works, but imagine it's dark, the alarm goes off and you now have an attacker within a 360-degree circle of you (and probably no more than 30 meters away). Not only that, but the alarm is not exactly quiet and can be heard if you are not wired in through a blast helmet.|Jatras, on the Cresh Luck Armor|<ref name="GG" />}}
The Cresh Luck Armor was a standard customization of [[Creshaldyne Industries/Legends|Creshaldyne Industries's]] [[MK.IV riot armor|Riot Armor]]. This battle armor<ref name="GG" /> covered &mdash;and protected&mdash; only the wearer's torso and front of his or her legs.<ref name="IA" />

The Cresh Luck Armor included a warning system known as [[Infrared Motion Sensor Array]]. This technology used [[infrared motion tracker]]s to detect any fast movement &mdash;which was understood as an attack against the wearer.<ref name="GG" /> Any object heavier than 10 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] moving faster than 1 [[Meter/Legends|meter]] per [[Standard second|second]] within a range of 30 meters triggered the alarm.<ref name="GGIA">''[[Galaxy Guide 10: Bounty Hunters]]''; [[Heavy Lifting]]''</ref> The default alarm was audible, but it could be configured to sound only inside a [[Blast helmet/Legends|blast helmet]], to become a visual signal in the wearer's goggles,<ref name="GG" /> or to be perceived as a subtle tingle. One user of the armor, [[Jatras]], believed that the audio alarm would either warn the attacker too, or prevent the wearer to pinpoint the attacker's position by hearing.<ref name="GU" />

==History==
{{Quote|It's a no-win situation.|Jatras, on the Cresh Luck Armor|<ref name="GG" />}}
The Cresh Luck Armor was available for 500 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="GG" /> It was one of the products in the illegal [[Gundark's Gear Datalog]], where several users &mdash;including Jatras and [[Heller]]&mdash; posted about the pros and cons of the item. Heller took the warning "[[tingler]]" of low charge in the power cells of the old [[DL-44 heavy blaster pistol/Legends|DL-44]] model of [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]] and adapted it to the Cresh Luck Armor, replacing the beeping sound with a less-intrusive tingle; after succeeding at this, Heller wrote about the method on the Datalog.<ref name="GU" />

During that War, a number of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] used Cresh Luck Armors.<ref name="GG10">''[[Galaxy Guide 10: Bounty Hunters]]''</ref> One of them was the relentless [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gennan Var]]. Var wore his Cresh Luck Armor when he was tracking [[Nawnam]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]].<ref name="IA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Cresh Luck Armor was first mentioned in ''[[Galaxy Guide 10: Bounty Hunters]]''. All the specific paragraphs about it were repeated in ''[[Gundark's Fantastic Technology: Personal Gear]]'', adding new information on it in the form of a exchange between Jatras and Heller. The role-playing stats say that the Cresh Luck Armor was more effective against energy damage, such as [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolts, than against physical damage, such as a punch. Albeit the sources say that it is a modified Riot Armor, the non-modified Riot Armor has yet to appear in canon.
